note: A = canonical path: denormalize the already-normalized EVAL tensor to [0,1] (tensor_to_pil, uint8) then open_clip preprocess re-normalizes. B = clean path: open_clip preprocess directly on the raw PIL. Both end at normalized pixels; the only difference is the uint8 rounding in A. Same 138 test images, DFN-CLIP ViT-L/14.
interpretation: The inverse-normalization step is the CORRECT denormalization of an already-normalized tensor (not a bug). Its uint8-rounding cost is bounded by these small deltas: cos(A,B)=0.90, C=1 probe 76.81% (canonical) vs 74.64% (clean) = -2.17pp, zero-shot best-template -0.7pp. The reported frozen-CLIP result (76.8%) is therefore robust to, and slightly favored by, the canonical path.
